reference.title: Lever Military Press (plate loaded)
reference.listing: Video (movement reference only; the page could not be fetched from the authoring environment (gymvisual.com refused the request), so the data sheet was not read and the movement follows the exercise name and standard coaching)
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe in as the handles come down, breathe out as you press overhead.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s down, short pause, about 1.3 s press

prescription.effort: Stop 1-3 reps short of failure (RIR 1-3, clinical opinion)
prescription.load: Plate load is user-chosen: start with light plates on the horns and press with the back on the pad.
prescription.progression: Add reps, then load; slower return

cues.text: Sit tall with the back on the pad and the feet flat; palms forward on the handles beside the shoulders, then press to the start overhead.
Breathe in and lower the handles along the arc until the hands are about level with the chin, elbows under the hands.
Pause at the shoulders with the ribs down and the back on the pad.
Breathe out and press up along the arc until the arms are long overhead.
Hold the arms long with the shoulders down from the ears.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back off the pad
mistakes.fix: Keep the ribs down and the back on the pad; lighten the plates.
Keep the forearms vertical under the handles.
Finish with the shoulders relaxed down.

kinematics.norm: From well bent at the shoulders to nearly straight overhead (clinical opinion)
From the upper arms about level with the shoulders to the arms overhead (clinical opinion)
Pronated: palms forward on horizontal handles (clinical opinion)

kinematics.setup: Pivot 120.8 cm high, -78.9 cm behind the shoulders
kinematics.peak: Lever swings 20.5°; hands within 0.78 cm of the arc
kinematics.norm: The handles ride an arc up and slightly back over the head (clinical opinion)
Seated with back support; seated pressing loads the deltoids with less trunk demand than standing (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2013)

kinematics.peak: 2 s down, 0.3 s pause, 1.3 s press
kinematics.norm: Controlled, about 2 s down and 1-1.5 s press (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #5068, Lever Military Press (plate loaded), video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)
Botton, Wilhelm, Ughini, Pinto and Lima 2013, electromyographical analysis of the deltoid between different strength training exercises (Medicina Sportiva 17(2):67-71)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Plate load is user-chosen: start light and press without arching off the pad.
Let the handles down to the stop under control before letting go.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: stop the press just short of straight arms or use a more forward seat position.
Low back discomfort: keep the back flat on the pad and the feet planted.
regressions: Seated dumbbell shoulder press with light dumbbells.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Prime mover: flexes and lifts the arm overhead (Botton 2013 for deltoid activity in presses).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Prime mover: flexes and lifts the arm overhead (Botton 2013 for deltoid activity in presses).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the arm with the front deltoid.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the arm with the front deltoid.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Rotates the shoulder blade upward near the top.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Rotates the shoulder blade upward near the top.
muscleNotes.pec_r: Upper fibres help at the bottom.
muscleNotes.pec_l: Upper fibres help at the bottom.
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the ribs down; back support reduces the demand (Saeterbakken and Fimland 2013).
